review.body:
### The problem

The first `{` after a function has started is read as its body. In an arrow
function without braces the body has started already, and a `{` in it opens
an object:

```js
function layout(vertical) {
  const box = f => vertical ? {x: f.a, y: f.b} : {x: f.b, y: f.a};
  return box;
}
function after() { return 1; }
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       3      2     34      0       3 box@2-4@a.js
       1      1      7      0       1 after@5-5@a.js
       3      1     13      1       5 layout@1-5@a.js
```

The first object is read as the body of `box`, which then ends at line 4 with
the `}` of `layout`; `layout` ends only at line 5, where `after` starts.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_functions.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript_states.py`. In the body of an arrow function
without braces, a `{` after an operator now opens an object. After an operand,
such as the type in `function f(): (e: E) => boolean {`, it still opens the
body. With the fix:

```
       1      2     30      0       1 box@2-2@a.js
       4      1     14      1       4 layout@1-4@a.js
       1      1      7      0       1 after@5-5@a.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_ES6_object_in_the_body_of_an_arrow_function` in
`test/test_languages/testES6.py`, in .js, .ts and .tsx: the example above
fails on `master` without the change; a second test checks that the `{` after
a function type still opens the body. The full suite passes on the branch:
`python -m pytest test` gives 1667 passed, 7 skipped. pycodestyle reports no
new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

Arrow functions with braces, and the body of a function after its return type.
Two other pull requests build on this one: #533 and
#534.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.

dependencies.body:
Depends on #531.

### The problem

An arrow function without braces ends at the end of its line, but only when
the first token of the next line reaches the rule that ends a statement, and
that token is counted as part of the function. Keywords, modifiers and
brackets are read before that rule, and a line that goes on with the
expression ends it all the same:

```js
function m(key, cursor) {
  switch (true) {
    case key.left:
      return () => cursor.prevWord()
    case key.right:
      return () => cursor.nextWord()
  }
}
const pick = (a, b) => a && b
  ? a
  : b || 0
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       2      2      6      0       2 (anonymous)@4-5@a.js
       2      1      6      0       2 (anonymous)@6-7@a.js
       6      2     31      2       8 m@1-8@a.js
       2      3     10      2       2 pick@9-10@a.js
```

The two arrow functions in `m` end one line late, and the first one takes the
`case` of the next line: `m` has a cyclomatic complexity of 2 instead of 3.
`pick` ends at line 10 and loses the `||` of line 11. A modifier does not end
the function either:

```js
class A {
  handler = () => 1
  async load() {
    return 1
  }
}
function after() { return 1 }
```

```
$ lizard b.js          # master, 01afe9c
       6      1     21      0       6 handler@2-7@b.js
```

`handler` takes the rest of the class and the function after it, so `load`
and `after` are not reported. Also, `const inc = x => x + 1` followed by a line
without a semicolon has NLOC 2 and one token more than with it.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_functions.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript_states.py`. The first token of a new line now
ends an arrow function without braces in every state, unless the line starts
with an operator such as `?`, `&&`, `+` or `.`, or the line before ends with
one; the end line, the NLOC, the token and the conditions of that first token
go to the function around it. With the fix:

```
       1      1      5      0       1 (anonymous)@4-4@a.js
       1      1      5      0       1 (anonymous)@6-6@a.js
       8      3     33      2       8 m@1-8@a.js
       3      4     15      2       3 pick@9-11@a.js

       1      1      4      0       1 handler@2-2@b.js
       3      1      6      0       3 load@3-5@b.js
       1      1      6      0       1 after@7-7@b.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_ES6_arrow_function_without_braces_on_many_lines` in
`test/test_languages/testES6.py`: 5 tests, all failing without the change. The
full suite passes on the branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1672 passed,
7 skipped. pycodestyle reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

A `;` or a `,` still ends the function as before. #525 makes an arrow function
without braces end at the enclosing `,`: this branch keeps that rule, and a
merge of the two passes the full suite, the tests of #525 included.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.

Depends on #531.

### The problem

An arrow function without braces in the first branch of a ternary goes on
after the colon of the ternary, and takes the second branch:

```js
function choose(strict, b) {
  const eq = strict ? (x, y) => x === y : (x, y) => x == y || b;
  return eq;
}
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       1      2     16      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.js
       4      2     22      2       4 choose@1-4@a.js
```

Only one arrow function is reported, with the `||` of the second one.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_functions.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript_states.py`. The colon of a ternary that was
opened before an arrow function without braces now ends it; a ternary inside
its body, `x => x ? 1 : 2`, keeps its colon. With the fix:

```
       1      1      4      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.js
       1      2      6      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.js
       4      2     29      2       4 choose@1-4@a.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_ES6_arrow_function_in_a_branch_of_a_ternary` in
`test/test_languages/testES6.py`, which fails without the change. The full
suite passes on the branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1668 passed,
7 skipped. pycodestyle reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

Ternaries inside the body of an arrow function, and ternaries outside arrow
functions.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.
